subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should the Telegram plugin add a public channel/account text or parse-mode config, and which values/defaults should be supported across sends, captions, edits, and streaming previews?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing parse mode changes a public config contract and affects Telegram rendering, escaping, rich-message compatibility, and security boundaries.

options.title: Add narrow plain/html config
options.body: Support the current HTML-compatible default plus an explicit plain/no-parse mode with account inheritance and complete outbound-funnel coverage.

options.title: Include broader Markdown/entity modes
options.body: Add MarkdownV2, raw HTML, or entity-array choices only with explicit escaping, custom emoji, and security review across all delivery paths.

options.title: Keep existing knobs only
options.body: Decline parse-mode config for now and continue improving `richMessages`, `markdown.tables`, and targeted formatter behavior instead.

recommendation.title: Add narrow plain/html config
recommendation.body: Support the current HTML-compatible default plus an explicit plain/no-parse mode with account inheritance and complete outbound-funnel coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest history signal for the original HTML-formatting decision, rich-message opt-in gate, and prior parse-mode product review context.
